This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user requested that I systematically read large amounts of context from the code-conductor project's documentation and wiki to test and trigger Claude's auto-compaction feature. The intent was to generate sufficient token consumption and context complexity to activate the automatic compression of earlier conversation turns while maintaining current working context. The user made this request in four sequential phases, each asking me to "continue reading files" or "read all wiki pages" to progressively build context load.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Claude's auto-compaction system: automatic compression of prior conversation context when token usage becomes substantial
   - Code-conductor: an orchestration framework for managing Claude Code workers
   - MCP (Model Context Protocol): tools and architecture used by code-conductor
   - Audit methodology: comprehensive code analysis using multiple "lenses" (board-pointer inventory, development history, cited identifiers, machine-specific references)
   - Wiki knowledge management: 556 structured pages of operational knowledge organized by scope (global, projects, workspaces)
   - FUSE-union architecture: container-based remote worker isolation using chroot and FUSE filesystems
   - Playbook system: workflow management framework with stages and gates
   - Mutation-verified coverage: testing approach that proves code coverage through mutation testing

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - /workspace/demo/audit-0410/lens-a.md (2,217 lines)
      - Comprehensive audit of board-pointer citations across the codebase
      - Identifies card IDs, epic references, and development-tracking apparatus
      - Documents rulings on which citations should be REMOVED, REWRITTEN, or KEPT as product mechanisms
   
   - /workspace/demo/audit-0410/lens-b.md (983 lines)
      - Audit of development-history prose in code and documentation
      - Contains 70 REWRITE-PRESENT-TENSE entries and 9 REMOVE entries

   - /workspace/demo/audit-0410/lens-c.md (351 lines)
      - Audit of cited identifiers and positions (path:line citations, branch names, criterion references)
      - Documents 23 path:line citations of which 76% are already stale/incorrect
      - Lists 81 criterion N references across the codebase pointing to undefined external specifications
   
   - /workspace/demo/audit-0410/lens-d.md (500+ lines)
      - Machine-specific references audit (paths, hostnames, usernames)
      - Rules against committing author-specific machine paths
      - Distinguishes between product mechanism (e.g., docker paths) and author environment leaks
   
   - /workspace/demo/audit-0410/lens-e.md (500+ lines)
      - Meta-audit analyzing the repository as work-in-progress vs. shipped product
      - Identifies 408 card ID occurrences across 156 files
      - Documents ordinal citations into external specs, bare stale aggregates, development-history prose
   
   - /workspace/demo/plans/conductor-role-definition.md (240 lines)
      - Strategy document for tightening the conductor role definition
      - Measured observations from 268 conductor sessions (2026-07-04 to 2026-08-23)
      - Defines 8 functional intents and orchestration approach
   
   - /workspace/demo/plans/code-conductor-stale-aggregates-inventory.md

      - 4 items marked ALREADY-WRONG, 19 marked FRAGILE
   
   - /workspace/demo/plans/HANDOVER-transparent-remote-worker.md (219 lines)
      - Handover document for FUSE-union chroot remote worker architecture
      - Documents decisions from 3 completed spikes (S1, S2, S3)
      - Lists architecture constraints, accepted risks, dead ends, unmeasured areas

   - /workspace/demo/wiki/ (556 pages, ~27,000 lines total)
      - Global scope: 469 pages across 8 knowledge families
        - conductor-mechanics: 74 operational practices for driving workers
        - worker-trust: claims verification and independence
        - git-and-merge: rebase, sync, push, rename hazards
        - tool-footguns: Bash tool (zsh), grep/rg/sed/find, git plumbing, make, hooks
        - host-environment: 21 container constraints and capabilities
        - claim-hygiene: 39 prose/evidence/measurement practices
        - design-judgment: change shape analysis
        - flake-and-timing: measuring flaky and timing behavior
      - Review craft: 5 families focused on mutation-verified coverage
        - assertion-vacuity: 27 tests that pass whether or not the code works
        - fixture-discrimination: 14 patterns of indiscriminating test fixtures
        - coverage-scope: 16 measurement practices
        - survivor-triage: 10 mutation verdict categories
        - mutation-runs: harness operation and verdict lifetime
      - Projects scope: 78 pages across 13 projects
        - code-conductor: 45 briefing practices for cc development
        - code-kanban: 12 board operations
        - code-mutant: 10 mutation testing practices
        - code-system-test: spike rig driving (2 pages)
        - TTD-Linux: 13 reverse-engineering practices
